title: What does XLS-20 specify for NFTs?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-20 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-20 specifies native non-fungible tokens and their minting, transfer-offer and burning mechanisms. [1]

NFTokenID identifies a token, while issuer-selected capabilities and ledger rules control its lifecycle. The standard's protocol metadata is distinct from an artwork, license or authenticity promise. Offers let owners and buyers express trading terms without making every listing a completed sale. Dynamic URI changes belong to separate feature work and must not be inferred from the original NFT standard alone. [1]

A published XLS document describes a design and its constraints; it is not by itself evidence that every network has enabled the corresponding amendment. Read the proposal status, dependencies and current network configuration together. Mainnet, Testnet and development networks can differ, and later fixes can change operational behavior. The source for XLS-20 was fetched directly from the public standards repository. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Final. [1] Author interpretation: use XLS-20 as a specification reference and verify the actual network capability before promising it to a customer. Keep documented design, local tests and validated transactions separate when describing evidence. This article explains the standard rather than claiming a new live deployment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
